Imbecile

IM-buh-suhl -- from Latin imbecillus, 'weak, feeble,' possibly literally 'without a supporting staff,' from in- ('not') + baculum ('a stick, staff'). · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Imbecile is a stupid or idiotic person.

Only an imbecile would ignore three separate weather warnings and go hiking on the exposed ridge anyway.

Worked Example

A driver ignores a clearly marked detour, gets stuck in wet cement, and then argues with the construction crew about who's at fault.

That stunning lack of basic sense, in someone who really should have known better, is exactly the kind of person imbecile describes.

How Imbecile Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

fool

fool: a person who acts unwisely or without good sense

dolt

dolt: a slow-witted or stupid person

Antonyms

genius

genius: a person of exceptional intellectual ability

sage

sage: a person of great wisdom, especially through experience

How Strong Is It? — fool → imbecile → dolt

fool vs. imbecile

fool vs. imbecile: Fool is much milder and more common than imbecile -- almost anyone can be called a fool for one bad decision, while imbecile is a harsher, more insulting word implying a deeper lack of sense.

dolt vs. imbecile

dolt vs. imbecile: Dolt is roughly as harsh as imbecile, both blunt insults for someone acting foolishly, though imbecile has an old clinical ring to it from its outdated historical use as a medical term.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — im-

Prefix — im-: not, lacking (the form in- takes before b) (Latin in-)

Root — becile

Root — becile: a supporting staff (from Latin baculum, 'a staff, walking stick', worn down on its way through French)

Put it together

Put it together: Im- ('not' -- the shape in- takes before b) + becile ('a supporting staff', from Latin baculum, worn down through French) spell imbecile. Latin imbecillus meant 'weak, feeble' -- likely literally 'without a supporting staff' -- and someone too weak to stand without a staff came to describe, centuries later, someone too weak-minded to think clearly.

Word Choice

This unit teaches Imbecile as a noun -- a foolish or idiotic person -- though it can also be used informally as an adjective, as in 'an imbecile decision.' Note that imbecile was once a real, now-outdated clinical classification; today it survives only as a strong, informal insult, and should be used carefully.
